narrative.overview:
The site is a single strip of cool thermal paper feeding down a near-black night. Persuasion happens in two registers that never mix: big, tight Bricolage Grotesque headlines and DM Sans prose stand on the night, while the facts are printed on the paper in an uppercase, condensed receipt mono, one dotted-leader line per thing the app really does. Screenshots and the film are not cards; they are slips laid on the roll, tilted a degree or two, hanging over the paper's right edge.

Density is that of a real receipt: tight line spacing, tabular figures, dashed rules between sections, a sawtooth tear where the paper breaks. Colour is almost absent. The night, the paper and the ink carry everything; lime is a signal, never a fill for its own sake. Motion is the printer's: lines print in left to right in stepped passes as each stretch of paper scrolls into view, and the highlighter swipes across the line that matters once it has printed.

On desktop the roll is a three-column grid (copy, strip, slips) with each section's copy sticky against its own stretch of paper. Below 1080px the roll tears into pieces: each section becomes copy, then slip, then a torn segment of paper, centred at strip width.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous paper strip (460px) on a night ground, centred in a three-column roll.
Two type worlds: display and prose on the night, condensed uppercase mono on the paper.
Lime as highlighter stroke and interactive signal only.
Evidence (screens, film) arrives as tilted slips clipped to the roll, with real drop shadows.
Motion is a stepped print-head pass; reduced motion gets the receipt already printed.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: On paper, lime appears only as a stroke behind ink, on at most one line per section plus the TOTAL. Lime is never text on paper and never a panel colour.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two surfaces: night and paper. No grey cards, no gradients-as-surfaces, no third ground.

rules.name: The Till Voice Rule
rules.body: Anything printed on paper is Martian Mono with tabular figures, uppercase except the small sentence-case notes, and every label-value pair is joined by a dotted leader. Nothing on the night uses the mono, and nothing on the paper uses Bricolage or DM Sans.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type is always 800 weight with negative tracking (-0.04em; -0.02em for document-page section heads) and line-height under 1.

rules.name: The Objects-Only Rule
rules.body: Only physical objects (slips, clips, the printer mouth, the play button) get shadows. Text blocks, the paper strip and the night never do.

dos: Do print every product fact on the paper as a mono line item with a dotted leader, and keep it literally true of the shipping app.
Do keep lime to one highlighted line per paper section, plus the TOTAL; on the night, to the headline's key phrase and interactive signals.
Do put text on lime in Night or Ink; lime is a fill behind dark text, never a text colour on paper.
Do bring screenshots and video in as tilted, clipped slips with the slip-lift shadow.
Do close the roll and every narrow-screen paper segment with the sawtooth tear.
Do show the receipt fully printed, with no clip-path or highlighter animation, under reduced motion or without JavaScript.
donts: Don't add a third surface: no grey or tinted cards, no feature-card grids, no panels on the night.
Don't warm the paper toward cream; it stays cool (paper token).
Don't set prose, headlines or nav in the receipt mono, or line items in Bricolage or DM Sans.
Don't shadow the paper strip, text blocks or the night.
Don't restyle, recolour or dim the official App Store badge.
